subject: Competitive replacement: detailed cost / packaging breakdown request
messages:
From: Eliot Rhodes <eliot.rhodes@novamed.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-06-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Replacement evaluation — pricing details requested

Avery,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency profile looked promising. As discussed internally, our procurement team has signaled a potential vendor swap if we can match the incumbent's blended unit cost and guarantee an uninterrupted rollout window.

They attached the RFP excerpt that highlights current pricing tiers and a special custom packaging clause (see attachment). Can Redwood provide a side-by-side: 1) per-token blended cost at our current run-rate (est. 9M tokens/mo), 2) suggested tiered discount thresholds, and 3) any onboarding credit or pilot concession for a 90-day pilot?

Also: the incumbent proffers a 6-month rollback clause with a partial credit for early termination. Procurement will need an equivalent safety net.

Can you get me a written comparison by EOD Monday?

Thanks,
Eli
Eliot Rhodes
Director, Cloud Procurement — Novamed
procurement@novamed.com

Attachment: novamed-rfp-excerpt.pdf (pdf)
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Eliot Rhodes <eliot.rhodes@novamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-06-29T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Replacement evaluation — pricing details requested

Eli — thanks, attaching a first pass (see pack) and looping in Marissa from commercial so we can crystallize concessions. Quick notes up top:

- Blended token match: we can approach the incumbent price at scale with a combination of a tiered volume discount + a 3-month onboarding credit applied as invoice offset.
- Rollback/safety: propose a 3-month operational credit and SLA-based credit triggers (downtime >99.5% window) rather than a straight time-based rollback clause.
- Packaging: we suggest a two-track package — "Core" (generation + embeddings, standard latency SLO) and "Enterprise+" (KV caching, dedicated pool, 24x7 support).

I'll send a line-item workbook in 90 minutes. Is there any procurement nuance I should call out (e.g., preferred billing currency, PO process)?

—Avery
Avery Johnson
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.ai
Attachment: proposed-pack-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-06-29T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Competitive replacement — pricing / packaging (internal)

Looping in Connor to validate runtime cost impact and to suggest an ops-friendly rollback wording. Connor — see Novamed's RFP excerpt (Avery attached). Key asks for pricing model:

- Provide a blended per-token figure at Novamed's reported usage (9M tokens/mo) for the Core and Enterprise+ tracks.
- Draft two concession constructs: (A) Pilot credit: 90-day credit equal to 50% of first-month estimated spend; (B) Onboarding service credit covering up to 120 engineer hours.
- Rollback: procurement wants a 6-month rollback. We should avoid open-ended financial exposure. Instead propose: 6-month assessment window + capped rollback credit (max $X) tied to integration progress milestones.

Connor — what uplift (if any) do we expect in GPU-hours and dedicated pool allocation for the Enterprise+ track? If you can provide a short delta table by 2pm, I can shape the commercial.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Deals | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-06-29T13:58:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Competitive replacement — pricing / packaging (internal)

Hi team — quick runtime delta:

- Core track (shared pools, standard quant profiles): incremental GPU hours over their current footprint estimated at +12% assuming similar prompt distribution. Blended per-token runtime cost: $0.0008/token at 9M tokens/mo (before discounts).
- Enterprise+ (dedicated pool with KV caching): +38% GPU hours due to reserved capacity and caching overhead; blended cost ~ $0.00105/token (before discounts).

Suggested concessions to hit incumbent parity while protecting economics:
1) Volume discount ladder: 9M–20M tokens: 8% off list; 20M–50M: 14%; 50M+: 20%
2) Pilot credit: invoice credit equal to 40% of first-month spend (capped at $35k) + 60 hours of onboarding service credit.
3) Rollback safety: 6-month observation window, capped rollback credit = 50% of onboarding credit + refund of unused prepaid reserved pool (cap $75k). Requires integration milestone signoffs at month 1 and month 3.

I can convert these into a redline for the commercial term sheet.

Connor
Connor O'Brien
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.ai
From: Eliot Rhodes <eliot.rhodes@novamed.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-06-30T14:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Replacement evaluation — pricing details requested

Avery / Marissa — thanks for the fast turnaround and the workbook. A few follow-ups from procurement and engineering:

1) Procurement likes the volume ladder but asks that the first-tier threshold be lowered to 7M tokens (their run-rate can dip). Can you confirm impact?
2) Engineering requests a guaranteed KV cache hit-rate of >= 65% for the Enterprise+ track during the pilot; otherwise they will not sign the milestone. Can you commit to that metric or propose an instrumentation plan?
3) Regarding rollback cap — procurement will want the dollar cap visible in the term sheet. The $75k cap seems reasonable as an initial placeholder; please include language about how refunds are calculated (unused prepaid reserved pool pro-rata).

If we can get an updated workbook and a short term-sheet redline that includes the rollback cap language and the 7M tier by tomorrow morning, procurement will fast-track to legal.

Best,
Eli
Eliot Rhodes
Director, Cloud Procurement — Novamed
procurement@novamed.com
